conditions: The source must bind the exact admitted Design result it consumes.
excludes: Generated views, calculated IDs and digests, validator decisions, owner approvals, and execution receipts.
includes: Author-controlled Work Pack meaning, requested effect, route bindings, and readiness configuration.

definitions.misuse_warning: A schema-valid source is not a generated Plan, an admitted Plan, or an execution-ready Work Pack.
definitions.promotion_boundary: The Invoke Plan owner must accept any later change to the canonical Plan source contract.
definitions.use_carefully: Do not copy calculated output fields back into the authoring source.

voices.domain_context: In Invoke Plan, this replaces scattered author-controlled fields across generated Work Pack files and receipts while retaining the current plan-execution-source v1 as migration evidence.
voices.formal: For one Plan candidate P, exactly one authored source S supplies all meaning-bearing inputs; every generated member of P must be a deterministic function of the exact bytes of S and its bound predecessor evidence.
voices.normative: The Plan authoring source is the sole machine-readable document whose authored fields state the proposed Work Pack, requested effect, route contracts, and readiness configuration for one Plan candidate.
voices.operational: Complete the source request, bind one admitted Design predecessor, author the canonical source into an absent file, and pass that file unchanged to the Plan compiler.
voices.plain_language: The one JSON file where we write what the Plan is supposed to contain before tools generate the rest.

conditions: Every bundle member comes from the same exact Plan authoring source and producer run.
excludes: Independent admission, implementation readiness, owner acceptance, task execution, and product mutation.
includes: Every required generated Plan file and the exact producer receipt for that generation.

definitions.misuse_warning: Generation success alone does not prove that the bundle is current or accepted by its consumers.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Only an accepted Plan successor contract may make this inventory canonical.
definitions.use_carefully: Name the exact bundle inventory and producer identity whenever this term is used as evidence.

voices.domain_context: The bundle contains the Work Pack and its supporting planning, layering, trace, and producer evidence; it is not the execution of that Work Pack.
voices.formal: Bundle B is a candidate for source S only when the required inventory is complete and each byte sequence in B equals the compiler projection of S under one declared producer identity.
voices.normative: A Plan candidate bundle is the complete ordered set of files deterministically generated from one exact Plan authoring source and its bound predecessor evidence.
voices.operational: Compile the exact source into an absent directory, verify the required inventory, and keep the stage receipt with the bundle for independent admission.
voices.plain_language: All Plan files produced together from one source, held for checking before anyone treats them as accepted.

conditions: The admission validator is a different executable identity from the Plan bundle producer.
excludes: Semantic invention, Design revision, owner acceptance, implementation readiness, execution authorization, and product mutation.
includes: Clean replay, exact inventory comparison, predecessor freshness, structural validation, and declared consumer results.

definitions.misuse_warning: Admission does not prove the Work Pack can execute safely and does not authorize any task.
definitions.promotion_boundary: The Invoke Plan owner owns the admitted inventory and consumer contract; execution owners retain later readiness decisions.
definitions.use_carefully: Treat admission as stale after any bound source, predecessor, producer, schema, inventory, or consumer change.

voices.domain_context: Plan admission sits after deterministic generation and before capability status. Work Pack Readiness Audit and Implementation Readiness remain separate later proofs.
voices.formal: Admission A(B,S) is current only when independent replay of S yields byte-equal B, required consumer checks pass, bound predecessor evidence is current, and the admitted inventory and producer identities equal the submitted ones.
voices.normative: Plan bundle admission is an independent point-in-time result that replays one exact Plan authoring source, compares every required bundle member, and runs the declared structural and consumer checks for that exact candidate.
voices.operational: Give the validator the exact candidate bundle; it must rehash inputs, replay generation in isolation, compare every file, collect all reachable blockers, and emit a separate receipt.
voices.plain_language: A second checker proves that this exact generated Plan still matches its source and works with the checks that depend on it.

conditions: Every positive axis is supported by current evidence owned by the producer or validator responsible for that axis.
excludes: A single generic PASS, inferred readiness, inferred acceptance, and inferred execution permission.
includes: Separate authored, admitted, readiness, acceptance, and execution-authority axes with exact receipt references.

definitions.misuse_warning: Artifact-authored or bundle-admitted status must never be presented as implementation-ready, accepted, or execution-authorized.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Each downstream owner controls only its evidence axis; no single resolver may manufacture missing authority.
definitions.use_carefully: Report each evidence axis and its exact receipt instead of summarizing the Plan with an untyped PASS.

voices.domain_context: Invoke uses this state to hand a Plan successor into later readiness and execution workflows without collapsing artifact PASS into permission to mutate a product.
voices.formal: For Plan P, evidence state E is a product of independent axes including authored, admitted, implementation-ready, owner-accepted, and execution-authorized; truth on one axis does not imply truth on another.
voices.normative: A Plan evidence state is the typed statement of the highest Plan claim established by exact current receipts, while preserving all later unproved or unauthorized states as separate fields.
voices.operational: Resolve status from the exact producer and admission receipts, then attach later readiness, acceptance, and execution evidence only to their own named axes.
voices.plain_language: A precise answer to what we have proved about the Plan so far, without turning 'written' into 'ready' or 'approved.'

conditions: The Plan binds one exact admitted Design predecessor.
excludes: Redesigning admitted decisions, executing tasks, accepting product changes, and granting mutation authority.
includes: Implementation objective, decomposition, ordering, evidence, gates, blockers, gaps, and handoff boundary.

definitions.misuse_warning: A Plan is not the implementation and does not authorize execution.
definitions.promotion_boundary: The Invoke Plan owner controls the successor Plan contract; Design ownership remains upstream.
definitions.use_carefully: Keep the Plan's implementation decisions within the admitted Design boundary.

voices.domain_context: Invoke Plan sits after Define and Design and before Implementation Readiness or Task Session; it authors executable planning evidence but performs no implementation mutation.
voices.formal: For admitted Design D, Plan P preserves D's decisions while projecting a finite Work Pack, decomposition graph, evidence obligations, gates, and one typed execution-entry boundary.
voices.normative: An Invoke Plan is a governed translation of one admitted Design into ordered, bounded, and verifiable implementation work without revising that Design or executing the work.
voices.operational: Bind one admitted Design, state the implementation objective and constraints, author the Work Pack and companion artifacts, validate their composition, and hand off only the selected execution entry.
voices.plain_language: The checked map from an approved design to the exact work people or agents can perform next.

conditions: Split views must agree with the Work Pack or the Work Pack gate blocks.
excludes: Layer philosophy owned by implementation layering and duplicated task details owned by split task files.
includes: Objective, slices, task and SWU manifests, validation, blockers, gaps, gates, state, and navigation.

definitions.misuse_warning: A Work Pack with placeholder task files or unresolved contradictions is not execution-ready.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan owns Work Pack authoring; execution owners consume but do not redefine it.
definitions.use_carefully: Do not let companion views become competing sources of execution state.

voices.domain_context: `WORK-PACK.md` remains source truth even when waves, task files, shared context, and an Execution Pack are split into companion files.
voices.formal: Work Pack W owns the objective, slice/task/SWU graph, validation strategy, residue, gates, active layer window, and links to useful split artifacts; conflicting projections force W's gate state to block.
voices.normative: A Work Pack is the source of truth for an Invoke Plan's executable decomposition and current planning state.
voices.operational: Use the Work Pack as the coordinator control panel, link each task and SWU to its owned contract, and update state only from exact evidence.
voices.plain_language: The main control file that says what work exists, where its instructions live, and what is ready or blocked.

conditions: Every slice maps to at least one Plan task.
excludes: Execution ordering, task instructions, and SWU atomicity.
includes: A coherent delivered behavior and its evaluation boundary.

definitions.misuse_warning: A slice may contain multiple independently executable units and is not automatically an SWU.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan owns slice composition within the admitted delivery boundary.
definitions.use_carefully: Do not use delivery slices as a substitute for dependency-aware waves.

voices.domain_context: Delivery slices organize Work Pack outcomes while waves organize execution and SWUs define atomic work.
voices.formal: Slice S groups one or more Plan tasks by delivered behavior; S does not determine execution order and need not be an atomic execution unit.
voices.normative: A delivery slice is one coherent outcome that can be demonstrated or evaluated as part of an Invoke Plan's implementation objective.
voices.operational: Group tasks under the smallest useful delivered outcome, name its acceptance evidence, and keep ordering in Plan waves.
voices.plain_language: A meaningful piece of the result we can show, separate from the order in which we build it.

conditions: Promotion cites evidence from the prior layer.
excludes: Task implementation details and execution status tracking.
includes: Layer question, mapped waves, promotion evidence, deferrals, and gate.

definitions.misuse_warning: Preference or elapsed work does not constitute layer-promotion evidence.

notation.meaning: Ordered implementation decision boundaries, not completion percentages.

definitions.promotion_boundary: Implementation Layering owns the L0-L3 method; Invoke Plan maps its work into that method.
definitions.use_carefully: Keep layer decisions separate from work status and task instructions.

voices.domain_context: `IMPLEMENTATION-LAYERING.md` governs L0-L3 decisions and waves but does not own task status or SWU contracts.
voices.formal: Layer L_i constrains its mapped waves and may advance to L_(i+1) only when L_i's named evidence satisfies its gate.
voices.normative: An implementation layer is one L0-L3 decision boundary that names the question being resolved, required promotion evidence, and deferred concerns.
voices.operational: State the layer question, mapped waves, required evidence, deferrals, and promotion gate without placing task instructions in the layer artifact.
voices.plain_language: A checkpoint in implementation where we answer one kind of question before taking on the next kind.

conditions: Wave order must not contradict task or SWU dependencies.
excludes: Detailed algorithms and source-of-truth SWU definitions.
includes: Layer mapping, ordering, dependencies, parallel boundaries, entry gate, and exit evidence.

definitions.misuse_warning: A wave must not duplicate or replace task and SWU execution contracts.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan owns wave topology; execution owners act only within an admitted selected unit.
definitions.use_carefully: Parallelize only units with satisfied dependencies and non-conflicting write scopes or an explicit merge plan.

voices.domain_context: Wave files own ordering and parallelization; task and SWU files retain detailed execution contracts.
voices.formal: Wave V is an ordered subgraph of the Work Pack whose members respect dependency and write-scope constraints and whose exit gate consumes all required evidence for V.
voices.normative: A Plan wave is a layer-aligned execution-order group that names included tasks and SWUs, dependencies, safe parallel work, entry conditions, and exit evidence.
voices.operational: Map the wave to one layer question, list tasks and SWUs in dependency order, mark safe parallelism, and bind entry and exit gates.
voices.plain_language: A batch of work that can proceed together after its prerequisites and before the next checkpoint.

conditions: A split task file must be a useful execution contract.
excludes: Unrelated task state and global Plan rationale.
includes: Objective, slice/layer mapping, dependencies, scope, SWUs, done criteria, validation, handoff, and synchronization.

definitions.misuse_warning: A task title or outcome without implementation and validation detail is not an executable contract.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan authors tasks; later execution owners report evidence without expanding their scope.
definitions.use_carefully: Split a task when its behaviors can be independently verified or assigned.

voices.domain_context: Split `TASK-*.md` files own task-local execution details and must not be title-only placeholders.
voices.formal: Task T belongs to at least one wave and delivery slice and owns a finite set of SWUs; every non-exempt SWU belongs to exactly one T.
voices.normative: A Plan task is one implementation responsibility with an objective, dependencies, write scope, done criteria, validation, and SWU decomposition when it is not already atomic.
voices.operational: Write a useful task contract, link its source context, declare dependencies and scope, decompose it into SWUs when needed, and name completion evidence.
voices.plain_language: One responsibility in the plan, detailed enough that its smaller work units can be assigned and checked.

conditions: The unit passes split analysis and has one independently reviewable acceptance boundary.
excludes: Multiple independently verifiable behaviors bundled for convenience.
includes: One primary behavior, one parent task, bounded scope, dependencies, completion criteria, validation, and handoff context.

definitions.misuse_warning: A task-shaped bundle of separable concerns is not an SWU.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan owns SWU contracts; execution owners may only execute the admitted selected unit.
definitions.use_carefully: Atomic means independently executable and reviewable, not merely small in line count.

voices.domain_context: SWUs are the preferred handoff boundary for Goal, Task Session, subagents, or a labeled local fallback.
voices.formal: SWU U has one parent task, one primary behavior, one bounded write scope, explicit dependencies, one independently reviewable acceptance boundary, and evidence that can establish U without establishing sibling units.
voices.normative: A Smallest Working Unit is the smallest independently executable and reviewable change or decision owned by exactly one Plan task.
voices.operational: Split plausible independent behaviors, then record the retained unit's objective, parent, dependencies, scope, context, done criteria, validation, owner recommendation, and handoff note.
voices.plain_language: The smallest piece of work that can be assigned, completed, and proved correct on its own.

conditions: Acceptance-critical missing detail blocks Plan handoff.
excludes: New architecture decisions that belong in Design and unrelated implementation choices.
includes: Algorithm or steps, interfaces, data flow, inputs, outputs, edge cases, failure handling, constraints, and validation.

definitions.misuse_warning: Naming a component or outcome is not an implementation detail contract.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan may detail implementation within admitted Design; Design owns architecture changes.
definitions.use_carefully: Escalate architecture choices back to Design instead of burying them in task detail.

voices.domain_context: Medium and high complexity Plan tasks require useful implementation-detail specifications rather than outcome-only prose.
voices.formal: Detail contract I(T) is sufficient only when a worker can derive T's implementation choices and validation surface without reopening the admitted Design or inventing acceptance-critical behavior.
voices.normative: An implementation detail contract records the concrete algorithm, interfaces, data flow, inputs, outputs, edge cases, failures, constraints, and checks required to make a Plan task executable.
voices.operational: For algorithmic or domain work, state steps or pseudocode, interfaces, data movement, edge cases, failures, constraints, and exact validation; block when missing detail changes acceptance.
voices.plain_language: The practical instructions that turn a task name into work someone can implement safely.

conditions: The obligation's timing matches when its required artifact can exist.
excludes: Unrunnable aspirations and future evidence represented as current PASS.
includes: Target, timing, command or review, expected result, evidence output, and failure owner.

definitions.misuse_warning: A planned command or fixture is not evidence that the obligation has passed.
definitions.promotion_boundary: The Plan declares obligations; the responsible validator or reviewer owns their results.
definitions.use_carefully: Separate checks by lifecycle timing and evidence owner.

voices.domain_context: Plan validation distinguishes pre-execution, post-produce, and post-apply checks so a validator is never required before its producing SWU runs.
voices.formal: Obligation O binds a target unit, execution timing, validation method, expected result, and evidence output; O is satisfied only by current observed evidence, never by planned future execution.
voices.normative: A validation obligation is one exact command, deterministic check, or reviewable observation required to prove a Plan unit or gate.
voices.operational: Name the exact check, when it can run, expected result, produced receipt or observation, and the owner responsible for resolving failure.
voices.plain_language: The specific check and result we need before we can say a piece of the Plan worked.

conditions: Every positive decision cites current evidence for the bound target.
excludes: Implicit approval and generic PASS without typed evidence.
includes: Named target, required evidence, accepted outcomes, decision, and blocker causes.

definitions.misuse_warning: A gate cannot infer missing evidence from a previous lifecycle PASS.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Each evidence owner controls its result; Invoke Plan composes but does not manufacture it.
definitions.use_carefully: Keep artifact admission, implementation readiness, acceptance, and execution authority in separate gates.

voices.domain_context: Plan gates control layer promotion, wave exit, Work Pack status, and execution handoff without converting confidence or prose into evidence.
voices.formal: Gate G(target,E) passes only when every required member of evidence set E is present, current, structurally valid, and semantically consistent with target; otherwise G blocks.
voices.normative: A Plan gate is a typed condition that consumes named evidence before a layer, wave, task, or handoff may advance.
voices.operational: Bind the gate to one target, enumerate required evidence and accepted results, evaluate all reachable checks, and block on missing, stale, failed, unknown, or contradictory evidence.
voices.plain_language: A checkpoint that opens only when the exact proof it asks for is present and valid.

conditions: The condition prevents a named current transition or claim.
excludes: Non-blocking future improvement and unowned vague concern.
includes: Cause, affected boundary, dependencies, owner, and repair route.

definitions.misuse_warning: Do not downgrade acceptance or safety blockers to gaps to preserve a PASS.
definitions.promotion_boundary: The named repair owner resolves the cause; the affected gate independently re-evaluates it.
definitions.use_carefully: State which exact claim or transition the blocker prevents.

voices.domain_context: Acceptance-critical ambiguity, missing evidence, invalid structure, dependency conflict, and unsafe execution scope are Plan blockers.
voices.formal: Blocker B names a cause, affected boundary, responsible owner, and repair route; while B is unresolved, every dependent decision is block or not_evaluable.
voices.normative: A Plan blocker is a known condition that prevents a bounded Plan state, selected unit, gate, or handoff from proceeding.
voices.operational: Record the exact cause, affected unit or gate, causal dependencies, owner, and repair route and stop the dependent transition.
voices.plain_language: A specific problem that must be fixed before this part of the Plan can move forward.

conditions: The current bounded claim remains valid without the missing item.
excludes: Conditions that already prevent acceptance, readiness, or safe execution.
includes: Missing item, non-blocking rationale, owner, repair route, and escalation condition.

definitions.misuse_warning: A gap label must not be used to hide a current blocker.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan records classification; the affected gate determines whether the condition blocks.
definitions.use_carefully: Reclassify the gap immediately when it affects the current acceptance or safety boundary.

voices.domain_context: Distill flags and non-acceptance-critical detail omissions may become Plan gaps; unsafe or acceptance-critical omissions may not.
voices.formal: Gap H names an affected future or optional boundary, owner, repair route, and escalation condition; if H affects current acceptance or safe execution, H reclassifies as a Plan blocker.
voices.normative: A Plan gap is known missing information or evidence that remains owned but does not prevent the current bounded Plan state from proceeding.
voices.operational: Record the missing item, current non-blocking rationale, owner, repair route, and exact condition that would make it blocking.
voices.plain_language: Something still missing that we can safely carry for now, with a named owner and a clear point where it would stop us.

conditions: The exact selected unit and its current evidence pass the installed entry validator.
excludes: Task execution, implicit successor selection, and broader mutation authority.
includes: Selected unit, dependencies, route, write and effect scope, evidence, timing, gate result, and stop conditions.

definitions.misuse_warning: A valid entry projection is not owner acceptance or permission to execute.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan authors the entry; Implementation Readiness and Task Session own later admission and execution.
definitions.use_carefully: Bind one exact selected unit; do not hand off an ambiguous task containing multiple unselected SWUs.

voices.domain_context: New mutation-capable Work Packs default to selected-unit admission at Task Session unless a full-frontier reason is explicitly recorded.
voices.formal: Entry E binds one task or SWU identity, dependencies, allowed capability/mode/target/write/effect/input/receipt tuple, timing policy, gate result, and continuation point; any mismatch blocks admission.
voices.normative: An execution entry is the exact selected unit, scope, route, evidence, admission timing, and stop conditions handed from Invoke Plan to an execution-readiness or Task Session owner.
voices.operational: Select one unit, bind its current contract and evidence, declare timing and allowed effects, validate the entry projection, and hand it to the named next owner without executing it in Plan.
voices.plain_language: The exact doorway from the Plan into execution: which unit, who may run it, what it may touch, and what proof is required first.

conditions: Every referenced unit and dependency agrees with the Work Pack graph.
excludes: Source-of-truth task details, SWU definitions, and independent execution state.
includes: Wave order, cross-task dependencies, stage coverage, closure obligations, and parallelization boundaries.

definitions.misuse_warning: Changing a task or SWU only in the Execution Pack creates contract drift and blocks handoff.
definitions.promotion_boundary: Invoke Plan owns the projection contract; Work Pack and task/SWU owners retain source truth.
definitions.use_carefully: Treat the Execution Pack as deterministic choreography, not a mutable competing plan.

voices.domain_context: `EXECUTION-PACK.md` helps medium/high complexity handoff while Work Pack and split task/SWU files retain normative execution detail.
voices.formal: Execution Pack X is a projection of Work Pack W's wave/task/SWU graph; X may add choreography annotations but every referenced unit and dependency must resolve unchanged to W or its owned split contract.
voices.normative: An Execution Pack is a medium/high-complexity choreography view that orders waves and cross-task dependencies and identifies safe parallel work without replacing Work Pack, task, or SWU source truth.
voices.operational: Generate the Execution Pack from the admitted Plan graph, show stage coverage and parallelization boundaries, and block when it disagrees with source contracts.
voices.plain_language: The coordination map for a larger Plan, showing what runs when without becoming a second set of task instructions.

semantic_applications.rationale: The canonical registry contains no term for the single authored machine input to the Plan successor pipeline.
The canonical registry has general artifact terms but no scoped term for the complete deterministic Plan output set.
No canonical term names an independent point-in-time replay of a generated Plan bundle while preserving later readiness gates.
The current Plan documents describe separate evidence ceilings, but the scoped state that preserves them has no canonical definition.
The canonical registry does not define the Invoke-local artifact that translates admitted Design into implementation work.
No canonical definition owns the Work Pack's role as the executable Plan source of truth.
The canonical registry has no scoped meaning for the outcome grouping used inside a Work Pack.
No canonical definition owns the Plan-local L0-L3 decision boundary and its promotion evidence.
The canonical registry has no term for the Plan-local execution-order group governed by implementation layers.
No canonical definition owns the executable responsibility and contract fields of an Invoke Plan task.
The canonical registry does not define the Plan-local atomic execution and review boundary represented by an SWU.
No canonical term owns the task-level detail required when a title or outcome cannot guide implementation safely.
The canonical registry has no Plan-local term for an exact check and the evidence it must produce.
No canonical definition owns the Plan-local evidence condition that controls advancement or handoff.
The canonical registry has no Plan-scoped meaning for a condition that must stop current advancement.
No canonical definition distinguishes an owned non-blocking Plan gap from an acceptance-critical blocker.
The canonical registry has no term for the exact Plan-to-execution boundary and its admission timing.
No canonical definition owns the choreography-only role and source-truth boundary of an Execution Pack.
